title: Password changes do not require password confirmation or re-authentication
reasoning: The route allows any authenticated request that can satisfy get_current_user to replace the account password by sending a new password only. Password changes are account takeover-sensitive operations; a stolen session token or API token can be escalated into persistent account control without knowing the existing password. Because the request schema has no current-password field and the handler never calls verify_password before hashing the replacement, this protection cannot be enforced at the route.
reproduction: Authenticate as a user, then send PUT /auth/me with JSON {"password":"newpassword123"}. The handler updates password_hash without requiring the previous password.
recommendation: Require the current password, a recent-login proof, or restrict password changes to a dedicated endpoint with explicit re-authentication. Keep profile email updates separate if they should remain low-friction.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for update_current_user, and the repository search did not find tests covering PUT /auth/me password-update authorization semantics.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an auth API test that verifies PUT /auth/me with only a new password is rejected, then verifies the password changes only when the current password or equivalent re-authentication proof is supplied.
minimumFixScope: Update UserUpdate or introduce a dedicated password-change request model, enforce current-password verification in update_current_user or a new route, and add route tests for success and rejection cases.
